records.title: Conveyor Jam and Obstruction
records.text:
Procedure ID: PROC-001
Title: Conveyor Jam and Obstruction
Fault codes: OVERCURRENT, LOW_RPM
Keywords: jam, obstruction, foreign object, stuck
Symptoms: Motor current rises while conveyor speed drops. A foreign object or trapped product may be visible.
Procedure:
1. Confirm the conveyor is stopped by the deterministic controller.
2. Keep restart authorization disabled while the obstruction remains unresolved.
3. Notify the operator and request a visual inspection.
4. Require an authorized person to follow the site's isolation and lockout procedure before any physical intervention.
5. After the obstruction is resolved by authorized personnel, obtain fresh sensor readings.
6. Require fault acknowledgement, successful interlock checks, and explicit operator approval before a simulated restart.
Restart policy: Never restart automatically based only on AI observations.

records.title: Motor Overheating
records.text:
Procedure ID: PROC-002
Title: Motor Overheating
Fault codes: OVERHEATING
Keywords: overheating, temperature, motor, heat
Symptoms: Motor temperature exceeds the simulated safety threshold.
Procedure:
1. Confirm the deterministic controller has stopped the machine.
2. Do not bypass temperature interlocks.
3. Notify authorized maintenance personnel.
4. Investigate possible overload, cooling problems, and abnormal operating conditions using approved site procedures.
5. Require fresh normal temperature readings and verified interlocks before requesting restart approval.
Restart policy: A temperature returning to normal does not automatically clear a latched fault.

records.title: High Vibration
records.text:
Procedure ID: PROC-003
Title: High Vibration
Fault codes: HIGH_VIBRATION
Keywords: vibration, bearing, alignment, mechanical
Symptoms: The simulated vibration measurement exceeds the configured limit.
Procedure:
1. Confirm the conveyor has stopped.
2. Do not attempt an automatic restart.
3. Request inspection by authorized maintenance personnel.
4. Check for possible alignment or bearing issues under approved maintenance procedures.
5. Require acceptable fresh readings and deterministic safety validation before restart approval.
Restart policy: AI cannot authorize operation while vibration faults are active.

records.title: Misaligned Product
records.text:
Procedure ID: PROC-004
Title: Misaligned Product
Fault codes: LOW_RPM
Keywords: misaligned, rotated, guide, product
Symptoms: A product appears rotated, displaced, or contacting a conveyor guide.
Procedure:
1. Record the visual observation as a suspected misalignment.
2. Confirm machine state using the deterministic controller.
3. Request operator inspection of the product and guide area.
4. Require approved isolation procedures before any physical adjustment.
5. Use fresh sensor readings and operator approval before any simulated restart.
Restart policy: Visual alignment alone does not establish safe restart conditions.

records.title: Emergency Stop and Guard Interlock
records.text:
Procedure ID: PROC-005
Title: Emergency Stop and Guard Interlock
Fault codes: EMERGENCY_STOP, GUARD_OPEN
Keywords: emergency, e-stop, guard, door, interlock
Symptoms: An emergency-stop input is active or the protective guard is open.
Procedure:
1. Maintain the stopped state.
2. Do not bypass the emergency-stop or guard interlock.
3. Require authorized personnel to determine why the safety device was activated.
4. Restore the safety device only after the underlying hazard has been addressed.
5. Require fault acknowledgement, interlock validation, and explicit approval before simulated restart.
Restart policy: Releasing an emergency stop or closing a guard never automatically restarts the conveyor.

records.title: Invalid or Stale Sensor Data
records.text:
Procedure ID: PROC-006
Title: Invalid or Stale Sensor Data
Fault codes: INVALID_SENSOR_DATA, STALE_SENSOR_DATA
Keywords: invalid, stale, sensor, missing, telemetry
Symptoms: Sensor readings are missing, invalid, inconsistent, or too old for a recovery decision.
Procedure:
1. Do not authorize restart using invalid or stale readings.
2. Request a fresh sensor acquisition.
3. Notify the operator if the sensor problem persists.
4. Validate the data and safety interlocks before requesting restart approval.
Restart policy: Missing or stale safety evidence must not be interpreted as a safe condition.
